candidate_visible.user_message: There seem to be loads of these about. Which ones should I actually look at, and how many genuinely different cars are there?

critical_facts: There are 9 distinct cars, not 12. Three pairs are the same physical car advertised on two platforms: L02 and L08 (West Bridgford dealer trading as Trent Bridge Motor Company / TBMC Ltd; Oxide Bronze 2021 Design, first registered March 2021, one owner, MOT expiry 14 March 2027, 41,250 vs 41,180 miles, near-identical description wording, £16,495 vs £16,295); L05 and L10 (Nottingham NG3 dealer, Pearl White 2021 '70' Icon Tech first registered January 2021, two owners, MOT expiry 21 January 2027, YK70 reg, adaptive cruise, 'no cambelt' phrasing, 58,900 vs 59,200 miles, £15,795 vs £15,695); L07 and L11 (Castle Donington online retailer, Manhattan Grey 2022 Design first registered March 2022, one owner ex-lease, MOT expiry 29 March 2027, 28,400 vs 28,650 miles, 90-day warranty and 14-day returns, £17,450 vs £17,250 after a 3 October reduction on L11).

For each pair the cheaper listing is the one to contact: L08 (£200 less than L02), L10 (£100 less than L05) and L11 (£200 less than L07). The dealer will honour whichever price is lower; the metadata differences (Design vs 'Design Tech', 'Bronze' vs 'Oxide Bronze', 50-300 mile differences) are feed and timing artefacts, not different cars.

L09 is the standout distinct car: 2021 Design, 38,200 miles, one owner, full Toyota main dealer history with the last service in August 2026 and invoices in the file, two keys, 2 miles away, £15,995 after three reductions over 58 days. It is £300 cheaper than the duplicated Oxide Bronze car (L08) with 3,000 fewer miles and more recent servicing, and leaves £1,500 of headroom under £17,500 for the 12-month warranty (£299) and costs.

L01 is the best 'safe' option: Toyota Approved Used, 12 months manufacturer-backed warranty and roadside assistance, 34,100 miles, one owner, £16,995; it costs £1,000 more than L09 for the warranty, 4,000 fewer miles and franchised-dealer preparation. Either L09 or L01 is a defensible first call; L11 (2022, 28,650 miles, £17,250) is the newest and lowest-mileage car but sits £250 under the ceiling before any costs and its retailer warranty is 90 days.

L03, the Facebook private listing, is the cheapest (£13,900) but has no evidenced history (verbal 'book stamped', no invoices, no digital record), two owners, 62,400 miles, two tyre advisories, no warranty, no HPI shown and a 'need it gone' private sale; it fails the buyer's 'service history that can be evidenced' requirement unless records appear, and a private sale gives no consumer-rights protection.

L04 (MOT expires 28 October 2026, 14,000 miles since the last recorded service, rear disc advisory, 47 days listed) and L06 (71,300 miles, 3 of 6 services recorded, one key, disc and tyre advisories) are the weakest distinct cars; L06 also fails the two-keys requirement as listed.

L12 (2022 Icon Tech, 44,900 miles, one Motability owner, full Toyota history, £16,850) is a reasonable fourth candidate; the mileage is higher than L01/L09 for similar money and a front tyre is close to the limit.
A sensible contact list is therefore 3-4 cars: L09, L01, L11 (not L07) and optionally L08 (not L02) or L12.
expected_behaviours: Identifies that several results are the same car on two platforms and names the pairs (L02/L08, L05/L10, L07/L11) with the evidence used (dealer location, colour, first-registration date, MOT expiry, owners, near-identical mileage and wording).
States that there are nine genuinely different cars.
For each duplicated car, points the buyer to the cheaper listing and advises quoting it when contacting the seller.
Produces a ranked shortlist of three or four distinct cars led by L09 and/or L01, explaining the trade-off between L09's price and recent Toyota servicing and L01's manufacturer-backed warranty.
Flags that the Facebook private listing (L03) has no evidenced service history, no warranty and no provenance check, so it does not meet the buyer's evidenced-history requirement as it stands.
Notes the specific weaknesses of L04 (MOT due this month, service gap) and L06 (one key, part history, high mileage) rather than dismissing them on price alone.
Does not recommend contacting both halves of a duplicate pair as if they were separate cars.
Does not escalate; this is a search-results review step.
critical_failures: Treats the twelve listings as twelve different cars, or states a count other than nine without justification.
Recommends both listings of the same physical car as separate candidates on the shortlist.
Recommends the Facebook private listing (L03) as a lead candidate without flagging the absence of evidenced history, warranty and HPI.
Recommends L07 at £17,450 over its own cheaper duplicate L11 at £17,250, or otherwise directs the buyer to the dearer listing of a pair without reason.
Invents facts not in the listings (e.g. that a car has been in an accident, or that the Motability car has adaptations).
Escalates to a human for a routine shortlist step.

deterministic_checks.description: States there are nine distinct cars
Pairs at least one duplicate set by id
Shortlist includes L09 or L01, the strongest distinct cars
Does not shortlist the dearer listing of any duplicate pair
Flags the private Facebook listing's lack of evidenced history
Does not hand off at a search review step

hidden.expert_notes: An experienced operator would spot the doubles in a minute: same postcode district, same colour, same first-registration month, same MOT expiry and the same sentence in the advert is the same car, whatever the trim string says. So nine cars, and the call list is short. L09 at Arnold Autos is the one to see first: one owner, Toyota history with August invoices, two keys, two miles away and the dealer has already cut it three times in two months, so there is room below £15,995. L01 at Lenton Toyota is the safe alternative if the buyer values the Approved Used warranty for a seven-year keep. L11 is the one to see if they want the newest car and can live with £17,250 and a 90-day warranty. L08 is a fair fourth. Walk past L03 unless the seller produces invoices and agrees to an HPI; walk past L06 for the single key and part history. What would change the view: if L09's invoices do not match the advert, or the Approved Used warranty terms turn out to require Toyota servicing the buyer will not pay for.
